prompt: Parse --key=value options out of a String[] of arguments. valueOf returns the text after the first '=', and intValueOf parses it with a fallback.
explanation: Building the prefix "--" + key + "=" once and testing it with startsWith handles three of the rules at a stroke: a bare --key never matches because it lacks the '=', an empty value matches and yields "", and substring(prefix.length()) keeps everything after the first '=' so a value containing another '=' survives intact. Returning from inside the loop means the first match wins. intValueOf layers on top: null means missing, and Integer.parseInt throwing NumberFormatException means unparsable, so both fall back to the supplied default.
hints: String has startsWith(prefix) and substring(int fromIndex) -- together they are the whole of valueOf.
Return as soon as you find a match so a later duplicate key cannot override it; return null after the loop ends.
In intValueOf, check for null first, then wrap Integer.parseInt in try { ... } catch (NumberFormatException ex) { return fallback; }.
